rule: Open plains and savanna. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot, and a road through the terrain doubles that.
Rolling or rugged hills. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour, or 2 miles per hour through the gentlest rolling country.
Woodland. Light forest allows 2 miles per hour; dense, trackless forest slows travel to 1.5.
Sand or scrub desert. Travel is 2 miles per hour, and foraging is difficulty 12 or worse.
Marsh and bog. Travel is 1 mile per hour; the ground is difficult and conceals ruins and hidden paths.
Mountain country and broken highland. Travel is 0.5 miles per hour; passes are few and defended.
Shoreline and coastal water. A coastal road allows 3 miles per hour; a sailing ship makes about 6 miles per hour and can travel around the clock offshore.

name: Ruins
rule: Broken ancient ground. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour, and the rubble hides site entrances; exploring a site runs in 10-minute turns.
Cold, treeless ground. Travel is 2 miles per hour; exposure and scarce forage make long marches dangerous.
Crevasse-riven ice. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and a guide or ropes are needed to cross safely.
Ash slopes and lava country. Travel is 1 mile per hour; eruptions, poisonous air, and fires make the ground perilous.
Dense tropical forest. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and the canopy hides trails, ruins, and ambushes.
Open heath and peat bog. Travel is 2 miles per hour; mist and soft ground make navigation hard.
Wide grassy plain. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot, or 4 on horseback, with little cover.
Eroded gullies and broken rock. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; the country is easy to get lost in.
Tilled fields and hedgerows. Travel is 3 miles per hour; farm tracks count as roads for local journeys.
Open sea. A sailing ship makes about 6 miles per hour and can travel around the clock; small boats stay near shore.
Shallow coral water. A boat must be poled or rowed at 2 miles per hour; larger ships cannot cross.
An isolated shore and its hinterland. Travel is 2 miles per hour; leaving needs a boat or a ford.
Raised tableland with steep sides. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; climbing to or from the rim costs extra time.
Flowing water. Cross at a ford or bridge; travel along the bank is 3 miles per hour on foot.
Flower meadow and soft grass. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot.
Dark conifer forest. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; the canopy hides landmarks.
Sheer walls and a broken floor. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and the way down must be found.
Cracked white pan. Travel is 3 miles per hour when dry; there is no water or cover.
Cold ash and cinders. Travel is 2 miles per hour, and the air stings the throat.
Calm, shallow water. A rowed boat makes 2 miles per hour, and the shallows can be waded.
Rows of fruit trees and mown grass. Travel is 2 miles per hour between the trunks.
Wind-scoured upland. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; the weather turns quickly.
Deep, sucking bog. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and the ground must be tested ahead.
